searchDocs.title: Get​
searchDocs.content: </> Cache.Get() → {[string]: Sound }-- Every warmed template, keyed by name. Do not modify it. print(VluxySF.Cache.Get())

searchDocs.title: IsWarmed​
searchDocs.content: </> Cache.IsWarmed( soundName: string-- The sound name. ) → boolean-- Whether the sound is warmed. print(VluxySF.Cache.IsWarmed("MySound"))

searchDocs.title: Warm​
searchDocs.content: </> Cache.Warm( ...: string-- The sound names. ) → () Warms sounds by name. A name that is already warmed is skipped. A name that is not in the schema prints a warning. VluxySF.Cache.Warm("BossRoar", "BossStomp")

searchDocs.title: Chill​
searchDocs.content: </> Cache.Chill( ...: string-- The sound names. ) → () Chills sounds by name: their templates are destroyed. Sounds you already fetched are not affected. A name that is not warmed is ignored. VluxySF.Cache.Chill("BossRoar", "BossStomp")

searchDocs.title: Get​
searchDocs.content: </> Preload.Get() → {[string]: Sound }-- Every preloaded template, keyed by name. Do not modify it. print(VluxySF.Preload.Get())

searchDocs.title: Selected​
searchDocs.content: This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> Preload.Selected( ...: string-- The sound names. ) → () Preloads more sounds by name. Yields until they are loaded. A name that is already preloaded prints a warning. VluxySF.Preload.Selected("Footstep", "Jump")

searchDocs.title: ToDefinition​
searchDocs.content: </> Conversions.ToDefinition( sound: Sound -- The Sound to convert. ) → SoundDefinition-- The definition. Turns a Sound and its SoundEffect children into a SoundDefinition. Only properties that differ from the defaults are kept, plus the name. local definition = VluxySF.Conversions.ToDefinition(workspace.MySound) print(definition.Properties.Volume)

searchDocs.title: FromDefinition​
searchDocs.content: </> Conversions.FromDefinition( definition: SoundDefinition-- The definition to build. ) → Sound -- The new Sound. Builds a new, unparented Sound from a SoundDefinition. Effects are parented under their class names. local sound = VluxySF.Conversions.FromDefinition({ Properties = { Name = "MySound", SoundId = "rbxassetid://123456789", Volume = 0.5, }, Effects = { EchoSoundEffect = { Delay = 0.5 }, }, EffectsCount = 1, }) sound.Parent = workspace sound:Play()

searchDocs.title: Default​
searchDocs.content: </> Jitter.Default( center: number,-- The central value around which the jitter will occur. spread: number-- The maximum deviation from the center value. ) → () → number-- Generates the jitter value when called. Standard Jitter function that randomly varies from the center value +- the spread. local myJitter = Jitter.Default(1, 0.15) local sound1 = ... sound1.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets a random value. local sound2 = ... sound2.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets another random value.

searchDocs.title: Range​
searchDocs.content: </> Jitter.Range( min: number,-- The minimum value for the jitter range. max: number-- The maximum value for the jitter range. ) → () → number-- Generates the jitter value when called. Essentially just a random number that requires a specified range. local myJitter = Jitter.Range(0.85, 1.15) local sound1 = ... sound1.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets a random value. local sound2 = ... sound2.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets another random value.

searchDocs.title: Scale​
searchDocs.content: </> Jitter.Scale( spread: number-- The maximum deviation from the center value. ) → () → number-- Generates the jitter value when called. Very similar to Jitter.Default but the center value is 1. local myJitter = Jitter.Scale(0.15) local sound1 = ... sound1.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets a random value. local sound2 = ... sound2.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets another random value.

searchDocs.title: UnitLog​
searchDocs.content: </> Jitter.UnitLog( center: number,-- The central value around which the jitter will occur. spread: number-- The maximum deviation from the center value. ) → () → number-- Generates the jitter value when called. Produces jitter values with a shaped distribution that favors the center value. local myJitter = Jitter.UnitLog(1, 0.15) local sound1 = ... sound1.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets a random shaped value. local sound2 = ... sound2.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets another random shaped value. TIP This can be used to make more natural repetitious sounds like footsteps.

searchDocs.title: SoundSchema​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SoundSchema { SoundGroupContainer: SoundGroup -- Main SoundGroup for all other SoundGroups. SoundGroups: SoundGroups-- Dictionary of SoundGroups under the Main SoundGroup. UnattachedSounds: Configuration -- Configuration for Un-Parented Sounds. WarmedSounds: Configuration -- Configuration for Warmed Sounds. PreloadedSounds: Configuration -- Configuration for Preloaded Sounds. SoundDefinitions: SoundDefinitions-- Dictionary of SoundDefinitions. PreloadNames: {string}-- Names of the sounds the client preloads on startup. } The Schema for the library that is shared on client and server.

searchDocs.title: Get​
searchDocs.content: </> Schema.Get() → SoundSchema-- The frozen schema. Returns the full schema. Decodes every definition that has not been decoded yet. local schema = VluxySF.Schema.Get() print(schema.PreloadNames)

searchDocs.title: GetDefinitions​
searchDocs.content: </> Schema.GetDefinitions() → SoundDefinitions-- The frozen definitions. Returns every definition, keyed by sound name. Decodes every definition that has not been decoded yet. for name, definition in pairs(VluxySF.Schema.GetDefinitions()) do print(name, definition.EffectsCount) end

searchDocs.title: GetDefinition​
searchDocs.content: </> Schema.GetDefinition( definitionName: string-- The sound name. ) → SoundDefinition?-- The frozen definition, or nil. Returns one definition. Prints a warning when the name is not in the schema. local definition = VluxySF.Schema.GetDefinition("MySound") if definition then print(definition.Properties.SoundId) end

searchDocs.title: GetNames​
searchDocs.content: </> Schema.GetNames() → {string}-- A new array of every sound name. print(VluxySF.Schema.GetNames())

searchDocs.title: How it works​
searchDocs.content: You put your Sounds inside a Configuration named SOUNDS in ServerStorage.When the server starts, VluxySF reads every Sound and compiles it into a lightweight definition. All the definitions together are called the schema, stored as one compact buffer.The schema replicates to every client with the place. Clients do not request it from the server, so both sides can create any sound on demand from its name.  Because only definitions are stored, a Sound instance exists only while you are using it. That keeps memory low, and you can still preload the few sounds that have to be ready instantly.

searchDocs.title: Set it up​
searchDocs.content: Follow these pages in order and you will have sounds playing in a few minutes:  Installation: add the package with Wally.Folder Setup: build your SOUNDS Configuration in Studio.Initialization: start the library on the server and the client.Examples: fetch, play, and adjust your sounds.

searchDocs.title: Go further​
searchDocs.content: Advice: tips on using the library well and keeping sound memory low.API Docs: every function, with examples.

searchDocs.title: SoundGroups​
searchDocs.content: </> type SoundGroups = {[string]: SoundGroup } Dictionary of SoundGroups from the Schema.

searchDocs.title: SoundDefinitionInstanced​
searchDocs.content: </> type SoundDefinitionInstanced = Sound & SoundChildrenInstanced A Sound with SoundEffects parented.

searchDocs.title: SoundChildrenInstanced​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SoundChildrenInstanced { TremoloSoundEffect: TremoloSoundEffect? ReverbSoundEffect: ReverbSoundEffect? PitchShiftSoundEffect: PitchShiftSoundEffect? FlangeSoundEffect: FlangeSoundEffect? EqualizerSoundEffect: EqualizerSoundEffect? EchoSoundEffect: EchoSoundEffect? DistortionSoundEffect: DistortionSoundEffect? CompressorSoundEffect: CompressorSoundEffect? ChorusSoundEffect: ChorusSoundEffect? } All possible SoundEffects to find within a Sound.

searchDocs.title: Why does this library exist?​
searchDocs.content: This library is designed for fast iteration!  Finding a sound by walking folders takes several lines, and it errors when the sound moves or is removed. Fetching by name removes both problems.

searchDocs.title: How far does it scale?​
searchDocs.content: The schema is compiled on the server into a compact buffer and replicates to clients with the place, so a large sound library costs little at startup. Definitions are only decoded when they are asked for.  The practical limit is naming. There is no hierarchy when fetching sounds; it is completely flat. So the difficulty of giving every sound a unique name goes up as the number of sounds goes up.

searchDocs.title: Working with the library​
searchDocs.content: Set your sounds up in Studio for their most common use. Adjust each sound in edit mode, then use presets or change properties yourself for the small things that differ at runtime. If a sound ends up too different from its original copy, it may be better to make a new Sound, even if it has the same SoundId. Keep sounds out of game logic. Game code should not wait on a sound or branch on one. Fetch and play sounds from the code that already knows what happened. Gate code that runs before startup. Most of the API errors if it is used before Startup.InitServer or Startup.InitClient has run. Scripts that may run earlier should call VluxySF.Startup.WaitForSchema() or VluxySF.Startup.ConnectForSchema(callback) first. Start the client fast with InitClient(0). By default, Startup.InitClient yields until the tagged sounds preload or 5 seconds pass. If your game wants the fastest possible client start, pass 0: the call returns right away, the preloads still run in the background, and no timeout warning is printed. Check on them later with Startup.IsPreloaded() or Startup.WaitForPreload(). VluxySF.Startup.InitClient(0) -- Other startup work runs while the preloads download. VluxySF.Startup.WaitForPreload()

searchDocs.title: Memory optimizations​
searchDocs.content: Optimizing may be important if your game needs to run on phones or old devices.  In short:  Only preload the sounds that you know need it.Lazy load your sounds wherever possible.Destroy sounds when you don't need them for the moment.Use third party software like Audacity or FL Studio to compress your audio.

searchDocs.title: Preloading​
searchDocs.content: This library makes preloading easy, as you just need to tag a sound with VluxySF_Preload. But just because it's easy, that doesn't mean you should preload everything, especially if your game uses more than 20 sounds. The more sounds you preload, the more memory is taken up throughout the game.  warning There is no way to undo preloading a sound.  If a sound only has to be ready for a while, like the sounds of one map, warm it instead. You can chill it again once you are done.

searchDocs.title: Lazy loading​
searchDocs.content: Lazy loading means creating a sound only when it is needed. Call VluxySF.Fetch at the moment you need the sound, not ahead of time, and destroy it when you are done.

searchDocs.title: Destroying your sounds​
searchDocs.content: If you want to save more memory, destroy the sound made by VluxySF once you're done playing it. VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce does this for you automatically.  note Lazy loading and destroying only save memory if the SoundId was not preloaded and no other sound with the same SoundId exists.

searchDocs.title: Reading the schema​
searchDocs.content: VluxySF.Schema.Get() and VluxySF.Schema.GetDefinitions() decode every definition in the schema and keep them in memory. If you only need one, use VluxySF.Schema.GetDefinition(name), which decodes just that one.

searchDocs.title: Sound editing​
searchDocs.content: Editing your audio files should be a last resort, as it is the most tedious of these methods. There is also a monthly import limit for audio in Roblox. But this is the best way to save memory, if it's worth it to you.

searchDocs.title: When to optimize?​
searchDocs.content: Optimize sound memory when you have a reason to: a memory warning on a target device, or a polish pass before release. Until then, tag only the sounds that must be ready instantly and destroy sounds you are done with. The rest can wait.

searchDocs.content: </> SoundGroups.GetByName( name: string-- The group name. ) → SoundGroup? -- The SoundGroup, or nil. local music = VluxySF.Groups.GetByName("MUSIC") if music then music.Volume = 0.3 end

searchDocs.title: SetMainVolume​
searchDocs.content: </> SoundGroups.SetMainVolume( mainVolume: number-- The volume. ) → () Sets the volume of the main SoundGroup that every other group sits under. VluxySF.Groups.SetMainVolume(0.3)

searchDocs.content: </> SoundGroups.SetVolumes( mainVolume: number?,-- The main volume, or nil to leave it as it is. volumes: {[string]: number}-- Group volumes, keyed by group name. ) → () Sets several volumes at once. A group name that does not exist prints a warning and is skipped. VluxySF.Groups.SetVolumes(1, { MUSIC = 0.7, SFX = 0.5, }) VluxySF.Groups.SetVolumes(nil, { MUSIC = 0.2 }) -- Leaves the main volume alone.

searchDocs.title: 1. Add the package​
searchDocs.content: If your project does not use Wally yet, run wally init in your project directory first.  Then add VluxySF under [dependencies] in your wally.toml:  [package] name = "your_name/your_project" version = "0.1.0" registry = "https://github.com/UpliftGames/wally-index" realm = "shared" [dependencies] VluxySF = "greenviper126/vluxysf@^2"   Run wally install in your project. Wally creates a Packages folder that contains VluxySF.

searchDocs.title: Upgrading from 1.x​
searchDocs.content: Change the version to @^2 and run wally install again. Your code keeps working, with these differences:  Startup.InitClient(0) no longer waits for the preloads or warns. Other scripts waiting with WaitForSchema resume as soon as the schema arrives, before the preloads finish.Calling InitServer or InitClient twice throws an error.The companion VS Code extension is gone. Sound names are plain strings.  The full list is in the changelog.

searchDocs.title: 2. Sync the package into Studio​
searchDocs.content: VluxySF runs on both the server and the client, so the Packages folder has to be somewhere both can reach. ReplicatedStorage is the usual place.  Add the Packages folder to your Rojo project file:  { "name": "your_project", "tree": { "$className": "DataModel", "ReplicatedStorage": { "$className": "ReplicatedStorage", "Packages": { "$path": "Packages" } } } }

searchDocs.title: 3. Require it​
searchDocs.content: With the setup above, you can require the library from any script:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF)   Every example in these docs uses this path. If your Packages folder is somewhere else, change the path to match.

searchDocs.title: Next step​
searchDocs.content: The library needs sounds to work with. Continue to Folder Setup.

searchDocs.title: The basics​
searchDocs.content: Legend:  ⚙️ = Configuration Instance 📁 = Folder Instance 🔊 = Sound Instance   Example:  SOUNDS⚙️ ← The base Configuration ├─ MUSIC⚙️ ← Becomes the MUSIC SoundGroup │ ├─ mainTheme🔊 ← Grouped to MUSIC │ └─ battle🔊 ← Grouped to MUSIC └─ SFX⚙️ ← Becomes the SFX SoundGroup ├─ click🔊 ← Grouped to SFX └─ explosion🔊 ← Grouped to SFX   There are only three rules:  Every direct child of SOUNDS is a Configuration with a unique name. Each one becomes a SoundGroup with the same name. A Folder or Sound placed directly under SOUNDS, or two groups with the same name, makes InitServer throw an error.Every Sound goes inside one of those group Configurations. It is assigned to that SoundGroup automatically.Every Sound has a unique name. The name is the key you fetch it with, like VluxySF.Fetch("explosion"). If two sounds share a name, a warning is printed on the server and only the first one is kept.

searchDocs.title: Naming conventions​
searchDocs.content: Instance	Recommended	Required?SoundGroup Configurations	UPPER_CASE	No, any name works Folders	PascalCase	No, any name works Sounds	PascalCase or camelCase	No, but the name must be unique

searchDocs.title: Organizing with folders​
searchDocs.content: Inside a group you can use Folders (📁) however you like. Any other instance that is not a Sound, such as a nested Configuration or a Model, is treated the same way as a Folder.  SOUNDS⚙️ └─ SFX⚙️ ├─ UI📁 │ └─ click🔊 └─ Game📁 └─ explosion🔊   tip The hierarchy inside a group does not affect the library. Sounds are always fetched by name, so you can reorganize your folders at any time without touching your code.

searchDocs.title: Preloading sounds​
searchDocs.content: Want certain sounds to be ready instantly? Give an instance the tag VluxySF_Preload, and every Sound under it is preloaded when the client starts.  Tag a Sound to preload that one sound.Tag a Folder or any other container to preload every sound inside it.Tag a group Configuration to preload the whole group.  SOUNDS⚙️ ├─ MUSIC⚙️ │ ├─ mainTheme🔊 │ └─ battles📁 ← Tagged "VluxySF_Preload": both sounds inside preload │ ├─ importantSound1🔊 │ └─ importantSound2🔊 └─ SFX⚙️ ├─ click🔊 └─ explosions📁 ├─ commonExplosion🔊 ← Tagged "VluxySF_Preload": only this sound preloads └─ uncommonLongExplosion🔊   You can add a tag in Studio from the Tags section at the bottom of the Properties window.  warning Only preload the sounds that need it. A preloaded sound stays in memory for the whole session, and there is no way to undo it. See Advice for more.

searchDocs.title: Preload timeout​
searchDocs.content: InitClient yields until the tagged sounds are preloaded or the timeout passes. The timeout is in seconds and defaults to 5. If the timeout passes first, a warning is printed, InitClient returns, and the sounds keep loading in the background.  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) local preloadTimeout = 10 VluxySF.Startup.InitClient(preloadTimeout) -- Reaches this line once the sounds are preloaded or the timeout is reached.   Pass 0 to not wait at all. No warning is printed. Check on the preloads later with Startup.IsPreloaded() or Startup.WaitForPreload().  VluxySF.Startup.InitClient(0) -- Do other startup work here. VluxySF.Startup.WaitForPreload()   See Startup for the full reference.

searchDocs.title: Configuring sounds​
searchDocs.content: Set up each Sound in Studio exactly how you want it to play.  Properties: Set SoundId, Volume, PlaybackSpeed, and so on directly on the Sound. A fetched sound comes out the way you authored it. Parent, Archivable, attributes, tags, read-only state such as IsPlaying and TimeLength, and deprecated properties such as Pitch, MinDistance, MaxDistance and EmitterSize are not kept.Effects: Add effects such as EqualizerSoundEffect or ReverbSoundEffect as children of the Sound.  note Only SoundEffects are kept. Any other instance parented to a Sound is skipped with a warning.Only one effect of each class is kept per Sound. Extra ones are skipped with a warning.A fetched effect is named after its class, so you can always reach it with sound.EchoSoundEffect, whatever it was called in Studio.A SoundEffect cannot have children. Children are not kept, and a warning is printed.

searchDocs.title: End result​
searchDocs.content: When you are done, your SOUNDS Configuration should look something like this in Studio:    note Keep the SOUNDS Configuration in ServerStorage so it never replicates to clients. InitServer takes the Configuration as an argument, so where exactly it sits is up to you.  Once InitServer has compiled it, the Configuration is detached right away and destroyed shortly after, once the calling thread yields or finishes. Nothing else should read from it after that.

searchDocs.title: Next step​
searchDocs.content: Your sounds are ready. Continue to Initialization to start the library.

searchDocs.title: Fetch​
searchDocs.content: RequiresSchema </> VluxySF.Fetch( name: string,-- The name of the Sound. parent: Instance? ,-- Parent of the Sound. preset: ((Sound ) → ())?-- Preset to apply before parenting. ) → Sound -- The new Sound. Creates the Sound with that name. If the name is not in the schema, a warning is printed and a blank Sound named VluxySF_Blank_Sound is returned instead, so calling code never has to nil-check. INFO A preloaded or warmed sound is cloned from its template, which is faster than building it. A sound fetched without a parent is placed in SoundService.UnattachedSounds. local mySound = VluxySF.Fetch("MySound") mySound.Volume = 0.3 local echo = mySound.EchoSoundEffect if echo then echo.WetLevel = 1.3 end mySound:Play()

searchDocs.title: FetchStrict​
searchDocs.content: RequiresSchema </> VluxySF.FetchStrict( name: string,-- The name of the Sound. parent: Instance? ,-- Parent of the Sound. preset: ((Sound ) → ())?-- Preset to apply before parenting. ) → Sound? -- The new Sound, or nil. The same as Fetch, but returns nil instead of a blank sound when the name is not in the schema. local mySound = VluxySF.FetchStrict("MySound") if mySound then mySound:Play() end

searchDocs.title: FetchPlayOnce​
searchDocs.content: RequiresSchema </> VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce( name: string,-- The name of the Sound. parent: Instance? ,-- Parent of the Sound. preset: ((Sound ) → ())?,-- Preset to apply before parenting. waitOnLoad: boolean?-- Wait for the Sound to load before playing. The wait never blocks the caller. ) → () → ()-- Stops and destroys the Sound early. Fetches a Sound, plays it once, and destroys it when it ends. Looping is turned off. If the name is not in the schema, a warning is printed, nothing plays, and nothing is left behind. VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("MySound")

searchDocs.title: InitServer​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Startup.InitServer( soundFolder: Configuration -- The SOUNDS Configuration. ) → () Compiles the SOUNDS Configuration into the schema, publishes it to clients, and destroys the Configuration. DANGER Call this once. The schema is locked after it is built, so sounds and SoundGroups cannot be added while the game runs. local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) VluxySF.Startup.InitServer(ServerStorage.SOUNDS)

searchDocs.title: InitClient​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> Startup.InitClient( timeout: number?-- How long to wait for the preloads, in seconds. Default is 5. 0 does not wait. ) → () Receives the schema from the server, then builds and preloads every sound tagged for preloading. The schema is ready as soon as it is received, so WaitForSchema and ConnectForSchema in other scripts resume then. This call itself yields until the preloads finish or timeout seconds pass, whichever comes first, and warns if it timed out. Pass 0 to not wait at all: the preloads still run in the background, no warning is printed, and you can check on them with IsPreloaded or WaitForPreload. DANGER Call this once per client. local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) VluxySF.Startup.InitClient(4)

searchDocs.title: IsInitialized​
searchDocs.content: </> Startup.IsInitialized() → boolean-- Whether the schema is ready on this side. print(VluxySF.Startup.IsInitialized())

searchDocs.title: WaitForSchema​
searchDocs.content: This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> Startup.WaitForSchema() → () Yields until the schema is ready. Returns right away if it already is. VluxySF.Startup.WaitForSchema() VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("MySound")

searchDocs.title: ConnectForSchema​
searchDocs.content: </> Startup.ConnectForSchema( finished: () → ()-- Runs when the schema is ready. ) → () → ()-- Cancels the callback if it has not run yet. Runs the callback once the schema is ready, without yielding. If it already is, the callback runs in a new thread right away. VluxySF.Startup.ConnectForSchema(function() VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("MySound") end) -- This line does not wait.

searchDocs.title: IsPreloaded​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> Startup.IsPreloaded() → boolean-- Whether the sounds tagged for preloading have finished loading. print(VluxySF.Startup.IsPreloaded())

searchDocs.title: WaitForPreload​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> Startup.WaitForPreload() → () Yields until the sounds tagged for preloading have finished loading. Returns right away if they have. Useful after InitClient(0). VluxySF.Startup.InitClient(0) -- Do other startup work here. VluxySF.Startup.WaitForPreload()

searchDocs.title: 1. Start the server​
searchDocs.content: In a server script, give the library your SOUNDS Configuration:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) VluxySF.Startup.InitServer(ServerStorage.SOUNDS) -- The schema can be used from here on.   InitServer compiles every sound into the schema and publishes it. Clients receive the schema when they join, so nothing is requested from the server at runtime.  info InitServer detaches the SOUNDS Configuration right away and destroys it shortly after, once the calling thread yields or finishes. Your Configuration in Studio is not changed. The schema is locked once it is created, so sounds and SoundGroups cannot be added while the game is running.

searchDocs.title: 2. Start the client​
searchDocs.content: In a client script, the setup is very similar:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) VluxySF.Startup.InitClient() -- Yields until the tagged sounds are preloaded, or 5 seconds pass. -- The schema can be used from here on.   InitClient receives the schema, then builds and preloads the sounds you tagged for preloading.

searchDocs.title: The preload timeout​
searchDocs.content: InitClient takes one optional argument: how many seconds to wait for the preloads. The default is 5.  InitClient() or InitClient(seconds) yields until the preloads finish or the timeout passes, whichever comes first. If it timed out, a warning is printed and the preloads keep going in the background.InitClient(0) does not wait for the preloads at all. No warning is printed. The preloads still run in the background.A negative timeout throws an error.  Either way, the schema is ready as soon as it is received, before the preload wait. Other scripts waiting with WaitForSchema resume at that point, even while InitClient is still waiting for the preloads. Fetching a sound that is still preloading works; the engine finishes loading it when it plays.  When you do not wait, Startup.IsPreloaded() tells you whether the tagged sounds have finished loading, and Startup.WaitForPreload() yields until they have:  VluxySF.Startup.InitClient(0) -- Does not wait for the preloads. -- Do other startup work here. print(VluxySF.Startup.IsPreloaded()) -- true or false VluxySF.Startup.WaitForPreload() -- Yields until the tagged sounds are loaded.   Both functions are client only. WaitForPreload returns right away if the preloads are already done.  danger Call InitServer once on the server and InitClient once on each client. Calling either one twice throws an error.

searchDocs.title: 3. Use it from other scripts​
searchDocs.content: Most functions in the library throw an error when they are used before the schema is ready. Any script that is not the one that started the library should wait for the schema first:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) VluxySF.Startup.WaitForSchema() -- Yields until the schema is ready. -- The schema can be used from here on.   If you do not want your script to yield, use ConnectForSchema. It runs the callback once the schema is ready, or right away in a new thread if it already is. It returns a function that cancels the callback if it has not run yet:  local cancel = VluxySF.Startup.ConnectForSchema(function() VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("LoFiBeat1") end) -- This line runs right away.   tip If you are certain your code runs after the schema is loaded, you do not need to wait at all. VluxySF.Startup.IsInitialized() tells you whether it is ready.  See Startup for every function on this page.

searchDocs.title: Advanced: start it from a module loader​
searchDocs.content: If your game loads its modules in phases, like Init and then Start, you can start VluxySF during Init. Everything that runs on Start or later can then use the schema without waiting.  You have to bring your own module loader for this. This is commonly called a single script architecture.  Server module that starts the library:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) local Orchestrator = {} function Orchestrator.Init() VluxySF.Startup.InitServer(ServerStorage.SOUNDS) end function Orchestrator.Start() -- The schema can be used here. end return Orchestrator   Client module that starts the library:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) local Orchestrator = {} function Orchestrator.Init() VluxySF.Startup.InitClient() -- Yields until the tagged sounds are preloaded, or 5 seconds pass. end function Orchestrator.Start() -- The schema can be used here. end return Orchestrator   Any other module:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) local MyModule = {} function MyModule.Start() -- The schema can be used here, without WaitForSchema. end return MyModule   note This only works if your loader finishes every Init before it runs any Start. Sub modules can use the schema too, as long as they run on Start or after. If your loader does not want Init to yield, call InitClient(0) there instead and use WaitForPreload later where the preloaded sounds matter.

searchDocs.title: Next step​
searchDocs.content: The library is running. Continue to Examples to start playing sounds.

searchDocs.title: SoundDefinitions​
searchDocs.content: </> type SoundDefinitions = {[string]: SoundDefinition} A dictionary of sound names for fetching SoundDefinitions.

searchDocs.content: </> interface SoundDefinition { Properties: SoundSerialized-- Properties of the sound. Effects: SoundChildrenSerialized-- Individual SoundEffects and their Properties. EffectsCount: number-- Amount of SoundEffects in the SoundDefinition. } Fully Serialized Sound.

searchDocs.title: Combine​
searchDocs.content: </> SoundPresets.Combine( ...: (Sound ) → ()-- Your Preset Closures to combine. ) → (Sound ) → ()-- Closure of the combined presets. Combines presets together into 1 reusable preset. INFO Presets are applied in sequence from first to last. local myCombinedPreset = SoundPresets.Combine( SoundPresets.NaturalPlaybackJitter(0.8, 0.1), SoundPresets.NaturalVolumeJitter(0.7, 0.15) ) local myCombinedPreset2 = SoundPresets.Combine( myCombinedPreset, SoundPresets.Parent(workspace.Sounds) ) local sound1 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound1", nil, myCombinedPreset) local sound2 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound2", nil, myCombinedPreset) local sound3 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound3", nil, myCombinedPreset2) local sound4 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound4", nil, myCombinedPreset2)

searchDocs.title: Fetch​
searchDocs.content: This is the main function of the library! It builds your sound on request and always gives you a Sound.  local sound = VluxySF.Fetch("LoFiBeat1") -- Always returns a Sound. -- Do stuff here / adjust properties. sound:Play()   If the name is not in the schema, a warning appears and a blank Sound named VluxySF_Blank_Sound is returned instead, so your code keeps running.

searchDocs.title: FetchStrict​
searchDocs.content: Use FetchStrict if you would rather get nil than a blank Sound when the name is not in the schema. It still prints a warning.  local sound = VluxySF.FetchStrict("LoFiBeat1") -- Can return nil. if sound then -- Do stuff here / adjust properties. sound:Play() end

searchDocs.title: FetchPlayOnce​
searchDocs.content: If you just need a one shot, FetchPlayOnce fetches the sound, plays it once, and destroys it when it ends. Looping is turned off. If the name is not in the schema, it warns and plays nothing.  VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("LoFiBeat1")   It returns a cleanup function that you can call to stop and destroy the sound early:  local stopSound = VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("LongExplosion1") task.wait(1) stopSound()   The fourth argument waits for the sound to load before playing it. The wait happens in the background, so your script does not yield.  VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("LongExplosion1", nil, nil, true) -- Plays once the asset is loaded.

searchDocs.title: Choosing a parent​
searchDocs.content: The second argument of every fetch function is the parent. Give it a BasePart or an Attachment to play the sound in 3D space.  local door = workspace.Door VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("DoorCreak1", door) -- Plays from the door.   info A sound that is fetched without a parent is placed in a Configuration named UnattachedSounds inside SoundService. It stays there until you destroy it, so call sound:Destroy() once you are done with a sound you fetched yourself.

searchDocs.title: Presets​
searchDocs.content: A preset is a function that receives the Sound and changes it. Pass one as the third argument of a fetch function to set up the sound the same way every time. The preset runs before the sound is parented.  local presets = VluxySF.Presets -- Combine lets you merge multiple presets into one. local myPreset = presets.Combine( presets.NaturalVolumeJitter(0.8, 0.12), presets.NaturalPlaybackJitter(0.7, 0.09), presets.Parent(workspace) ) VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("RandomSound1", nil, myPreset) task.delay(0.1, function() VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("RandomSound1", nil, myPreset) end) -- This sound should use the same preset, but with a different parent. The parent argument wins over the preset. local sound = VluxySF.Fetch("RandomSound1", workspace.CurrentCamera, myPreset) -- This sound is different, but it should play in a similar way. local otherSound = VluxySF.Fetch("OtherRandomSound1", nil, myPreset)   The built in presets are Combine, Parent, Volume, PlaybackSpeed, NaturalVolumeJitter, NaturalPlaybackJitter, RandomVolumeJitter and RandomPlaybackJitter. See the SoundPresets API for each one.

searchDocs.title: Making your own presets​
searchDocs.content: A preset is any function that takes a Sound. Wrap it in another function when it needs settings:  local function randomName(name: string): (Sound) -> () return function(sound: Sound) sound.Name = name .. math.random() end end local myPreset = VluxySF.Presets.Combine( randomName("Footstep"), VluxySF.Presets.Volume(0.6) ) local sound = VluxySF.Fetch("Footstep1", nil, myPreset)   tip You can keep your own presets in a module and use them just like the built in ones.  note Combined presets are applied in order, from the first argument to the last.It is recommended that you only use presets to set properties and do similar one time work.

searchDocs.title: Jitter​
searchDocs.content: The jitter presets above are built from VluxySF.Jitter, which you can also use on its own. A jitter is a function that gives you a slightly different number each time you call it. Every jitter value is clamped from 0 to 10.  local pitchJitter = VluxySF.Jitter.UnitLog(1, 0.15) -- Stays close to 1. local function playFootstep() local sound = VluxySF.Fetch("Footstep1") sound.PlaybackSpeed = pitchJitter() sound:Play() end   Jitter.UnitLog favors values near the center, which makes repeated sounds like footsteps feel more natural. Jitter.Default spreads evenly around a center, Jitter.Scale does the same around 1, and Jitter.Range picks a number between a minimum and a maximum. See the Jitter API for details.

searchDocs.title: SoundGroups​
searchDocs.content: Every group Configuration in your SOUNDS Configuration becomes a SoundGroup, and all of them sit under one main SoundGroup named SOUNDS in SoundService. That gives you a main volume and a volume for each group.  Volumes can be set on the server or the client. The client is recommended for player settings.  local mainVolume = 0.8 local groupVolumes = { GAME = 0.7, MUSIC = 0.55, SFX = 0.64, } local function onSettingsChanged() -- Do stuff here if you want, like clamping your values. A SoundGroup volume can go from 0 to 10. VluxySF.Groups.SetVolumes(mainVolume, groupVolumes) end onSettingsChanged()   tip Call this whenever a slider or setting changes to update the volumes live.  note The main volume is optional. Pass nil to leave it as it is.You only need to list the groups you want to change. A group name that does not exist prints a warning and is skipped.There are more functions for working with your SoundGroups. See the SoundGroups API.

searchDocs.title: Keeping sounds ready​
searchDocs.content: A sound that is fetched for the first time has to be created and loaded, which can take a moment. On the client, there are two ways to have a sound ready before you need it. Both keep a template of the sound, and Fetch clones the template instead of building a new one.

searchDocs.title: Preload​
searchDocs.content: A preloaded sound stays loaded for the whole session. The easiest way is to tag it in Studio, but you can also preload by name at runtime:  VluxySF.Preload.Selected("BossTheme1", "BossRoar1") -- Yields until they are loaded.   Sounds tagged in Studio are preloaded by Startup.InitClient. If you started the client with InitClient(0), check on them with Startup.IsPreloaded() or wait with Startup.WaitForPreload():  VluxySF.Startup.WaitForPreload() -- Yields until the tagged sounds are loaded.

searchDocs.title: Warm and chill​
searchDocs.content: Warming keeps a built sound around only for as long as you need it. Warm it before the moment it matters, and chill it afterwards to let it go.  VluxySF.Cache.Warm("BossTheme1", "BossRoar1") -- Built once, so fetches clone instead of build. -- Later, during the boss fight. VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("BossRoar1") -- The fight is over, so these sounds are not needed anymore. VluxySF.Cache.Chill("BossTheme1", "BossRoar1")   note Preload and Cache only work on the client.Warming does not download the sound's asset. The engine loads it the first time a Sound with that id plays, or when Preload is used.Chilling destroys the template. Sounds you already fetched are not affected.  See Advice for when to use each one.

searchDocs.title: Reading the schema​
searchDocs.content: You can read what the library knows about your sounds at any time.  print(VluxySF.Schema.GetNames()) -- Every sound name. print(VluxySF.Schema.GetDefinition("LoFiBeat1")) -- The stored properties and effects of one sound. print(VluxySF.Groups.GetNames()) -- Every SoundGroup name.   GetDefinition decodes one definition. Schema.Get() and Schema.GetDefinitions() decode every definition and freeze the table, so prefer GetDefinition when you only need one.
